item.title: 🚀 I open-sourced a no-code AI agent that speaks crypto Built on @solana and powered by DSPy, th...
item.description:
@undefined

🚀 I open-sourced a no-code AI agent that speaks crypto Built on @solana and powered by DSPy, this project lets anyone create wallets and send stablecoins (USDC, PYUSD, USDG) using natural language. 🧠 What’s DSPy? DSPy is a framework for building language-driven agents. You give it a few functions, describe the goal in plain English, and it figures out which function to call and in what order. No hardcoded logic, just reasoning. @DSPyOSS For example: “Create a new wallet and send it 2 USDC and 1 PYUSD. Return all of the new wallet balances comma delimited in the format [token]=[balance]. Format the balances to 3 decimal places.” "Also send the last wallet you just created 3 USDG too" It executes the full workflow behind the scenes. 💡 Why this matters: * For engineers: Quickly expose internal primitives to broader teams through language. * For PMs: Skip the dev queue. Explore and test on-chain flows without needing to write or understand code. * For crypto builders: Simplifies onboarding, automation, and user experience. 🛠️ This is a starter demo. The pattern can apply to any function an engineer makes available: wallet logic today, staking or compliance flows tomorrow. 📦 GitHub: https://t.co/0g6fn1GR8y See the README for full instructions and a working example. 🤓 Details for the brainiacs This starter GitHub repo currently supports the following primitive functions that can be orchestrated by the AI agent: * Creating a Solana wallet * Sign and broadcast transactions from a main configured wallet * Using the Solana Devnet faucet * Transferring SPL tokens (e.g., USDC) * Transferring Token-2022 tokens (e.g., USDG, PYUSD) * Creating Associated Token Accounts for SPL and Token-2022 tokens * Retrieving Solana wallet balances 🌟 If this sparks ideas for your team or product, I’d be interested to hear them. ♥️ Heart, repost, or comment on this post if you'd like me to expand the primitive functions of the agent on Solana or even write something similar for EVM.
